newsitem.title: ITALY: INSTANT VIEW - Italy Dec CPI seen at 2.6 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Italy Dec CPI seen at 2.6 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Following are analysts' comments on preliminary Italian consumer prices data from four sample cities which show Italian inflation running at 2.6 percent year on year and 0.1 percent month on month.

A Reuter poll showed analysts expected preliminary December CPI to grow at 2.6 percent year-on-year, the same as November's 2.6 percent, while they forecast month-on-month growth at 0.1 percent against November's 0.3 percent rise.
Sharda Persaud, economist at San Paolo in London told RFTV: "This number is pretty much in line with expectations. It leads the way for a Bank of Italy interest rate cut, probably this weekend."

Alessandro Fugnoli, economic strategist at Caboto in Milan, said: "I think the Bank of Italy is in no hurry to cut rates. They will cut when they see inflation coming down. Since there will probably be an uptick in inflation in the next few months, they will be very slow cutting rates -- more slow than the market thinks."
Six more sample cities, with a heavier weighting on the national index, will publish their preliminary data for December on Friday.

Lorenzo Codogno, chief economist at Bank of America in Milan said: "I think there is plenty of room (for interest rate cuts). In the near term we should see a 150 basis point cut by the end of the first quarter (1997)."
The discount rate currently stands at 7.5 percent. Milan newsroom +392-66102321
